title: Paranormal pours: YouTube Channel, Haunt Hops, documents ghostly brewery and haunted historic hotel
excerpt: WEST JEFFERSON — Brewmaster Jake Cullen noticed a balloon hovering near the ceiling after a recent birthday party at Boondocks’ Brew Haus on Jefferson Avenue.
content:
WEST JEFFERSON — Brewmaster Jake Cullen noticed a balloon hovering near the ceiling after a recent birthday party at Boondocks’ Brew Haus on Jefferson Avenue.

A brew assistant told Cullen they would need a 30-foot ladder to retrieve the leftover party favor.

Almost on a paranormal cue, the balloon began moving across the ceiling, dropped below the first I-beam, and moved to the next rafter to begin another ghostly descent before getting stuck again. The balloon repeated the spiritual spectacle, which by then had drawn the brew house staff’s attention, before settling at the top of a staircase leading to the attic and ominously bobbing up and down.

Although Cullen dismissed the paranormal and ghosts, he said watching the balloon’s eerie dance was a “definitive (hair-raising) event.” Cullen immediately popped the balloon before throwing it away, ending the ghost’s toying with the brewery’s staff.

Creepy encounters at the Brew Haus are about as common as their rotating seasonal crafts.

Staff often report a prevailing, foreboding feeling of “being watched” as they close the entertainment venue and guests exit into the cool autumn night after an evening of reverie.

Cullen said it’s not uncommon to catch a dark shadow out of the corner of his eye while brewing Boondock’s latest craft beer.

There are also stories of a “Lady in Red,” a spiritual service companion to the widely known “Lady in White” episodes common in almost every community.

After some independent sleuthing, Cullen determined that the “Lady in Red” was likely a deceased employee of Geno’s Restaurant, which inhabited the building before Boondocks purchased the aging structure to sling drinks instead of the Italian eatery’s famous garlic bread bites and cheesy pizza.

Restaurant bar manager Muriel Stevens also shared a story relayed from a coworker. Her fellow bartender recalled commenting about a noisy drink machine at the brew haus.

“This night, it (the machine) was more than usual; it was making a lot of noise,” Stevens said. “Serena said, ‘Wouldn’t it be something if that was the ghost?’ Then, everything stopped. It was dead silence. So, she was pretty freaked out about that.”

Cullen and Stevens shared their ghostly brew haus encounters with YouTuber Brett Clark, who produces and hosts the “Haunt Hops” channel, a growing ghost hunting and craft beer crossover, where Clark sits down with bar and distillery owners across the region to discuss beer and spirits — both of the intoxicating and mesmerizing variety.

A related TikTok video of ghostly happenings at the neighboring Tap Room also conjured comments about a menacing ghost named Charlie, who rambunctiously knocks down drying dishes.

Haunted Hotel

In another episode, Clark sat down with Historic West Jefferson Hotel Owner Mark Beck.

During the video, Beck told Clark that the hotel’s guests reported hearing footsteps on the roof. Beck said he knew the encounter was impossible because the roof is “locked down” and reinforced with soundproofing.

Still, Beck doesn’t discredit the building’s paranormal streak.

Built in 1916, the hotel was a booming social and economic hub during the town’s railroad heyday. He said renovating the building likely “unlocked” meaningful community memories.

Beck said he also found other relics during renovations. Many rooms had hidden doors in the baseboards that are hard to see. One of the hidden compartments had a stash of obscene magazines.

After interviewing staff at both West Jefferson locations, Clark said the Brew Haus had more spiritual emanations than the busier hotel.

“At The Brew Haus, I got a little more of a vibe there than at the hotel at the time,” Clark said. “When I was at the hotel, it felt more active with people coming in to dine, so there was a little more going on; you get a different vibe when a lot of people are around, different than when you’re alone. It seemed especially different to me on the second floor at Brew Haus; going into the attic felt different, and there was also a mannequin there.”

Clark filmed a similar video at the Glendale Springs Inn.

During the interview, he said viewers can see the staff and crew react to someone walking through the room.

“We were all like, ‘What was that?’ Clark recalled.

Clark said he rewatched the footage to make sure no one walked into their shot.

“No one came into (the inn) until 45 minutes after the interview,” he said. “It was pretty interesting.”

Clark’s ghostbusting over choice hops also took him to the Green Park Inn in Blowing Rock before it was demolished.

He eventually traveled to the Nuwray Hotel in Burnsville. He said the old inn has a “heavy history” as the “second oldest hotel in western North Carolina.

“It’s a really interesting historical place,” Clark said. “In one of the rooms, a man was stabbed nine times in the neck. They also have a ghost log that guests can write down the weird things they noticed before checking out.”

Click to youtube.com/@haunthops to watch the Brew Haus, Historic West Jefferson Hotel, Glendale Springs Inn, and other paranormal interviews.
